about: Inviting and the army: the 💌s, the leash and sigil weight, the bond, berries.

berries.what: Berries on the bushes of every area, which her creatures eat to evolve.

decisions.quote: tie the cost to strength
Double the amount of berries animals need to evolve
decisions.rest: cost.per halved from 7.25
the level gap of made the youth's 6, 8 and 16 for light, normal and strong species

decisions.quote: We can change 6/8/16=>3/4/8, and reduce berry spawns (keep the current cluster size but reduce frequency of clusters.)
decisions.rest: a youth showing a dot per berry eaten, two rows of 4 at most:: cost.per back to 7.25, so 3, 4 and 8, and bushesPerArea and perArea halved, half as many patches of the same size, the same share of their bushes in berry

decisions.quote: we can make the berry clusters bigger

decisions.rest: legends are the areas' own, never grown

berries.notes: Berries and evolving (Ed): every area has bushesPerArea berry bushes (normal bushes of that area) and perArea [min, max] berries on distinct ones at the start. Bushes grow in patches of patch.bushes [min, max] within patch.radius metres. Party animals (invited, not legends), following her or held at a sigil, take a berry on their way (Ed, v233): within detour metres of the line to where they're heading or of their sigil, never beyond their leash; they nip over, eat it (eatTime seconds) and carry on. The berry grows again at once on a free berry bush somewhere else on the map. A party animal evolves on the next bar line once it has eaten the berries its next level costs [1]: the fighting value it gains (cost.by "value": √(hp × dps), its species' strength included) at cost.per a berry, rounded, at least 1: so a berry buys the same fighting value for every species; one of normal strength costs 4 and 4 [2][3][4] ("power" would count hp × dps instead). Bigger patches since [5]: perArea and patch.bushes up a quarter to a half, so the first evolve's extra berry (2, was 1) and weaker species' one-berry minimum come out a little faster to feed than before. Evolving stops at adult [6].

berries.glow.what: How strongly a berry's soft halo glows.
berries.glow.notes: its soft halo's strength. B (debug) feeds the nearest party animal one berry. Babies [1]: a baby eats only when its sigil is put down with a berry within babyReach metres of it (following her, it never stops for one; when a baby's sigil is next to go down, the berries within babyReach of her glow brightly), and babyCost berries evolve it into a youth.

invites.what: The 💌 invite: on the ground she fires spinning love letters at creatures to win them over.

decisions.rest: issue #87

decisions.quote: base invite should be one envelope at a time (rebalance hits accordingly), they should arc a little and disappear when they hit the ground, go 50% further, 20% faster, and they should rotate by pitching instead of yawing

decisions.rest: balance, the overnight pass, with the wider level gap

invites.notes: The 💌 invite [1], replacing the proximity chat when on: on the ground she shoots spinning 💌s, aimed with the cursor (click fires) or the right stick (a trigger fires), or 1 toward the cursor. A burst is burst volleys burstGap seconds apart, each multiShot letters fanned over spread degrees, then cooldown seconds before the next; letters fly at speed m/s for range metres, turning toward the nearest invitable creature within homingRange metres and homingCone degrees of straight ahead at up to homing degrees a second, and land on one whose body comes within radius metres. Each hit adds amount to its affection; Round 11 [2]: one 💌 a shot (burst 1, multiShot 1), cooldown 0.55 (just over the old 0.5 s per-creature gap), hits [4, 9, 18, 36] so a meter fills in about the time it did with bursts of three (they gave one hit each 0.84 s); then [3] [4, 7, 14, 36]: the young and adults quicker to win over, so good play counts for more (a skilled player lasts about 2.5 minutes longer, a crude one no longer), range 33 (was 22) and speed 31.2 (was 26).

invites.arc.what: the height (m) its lob rises over the straight line from her hand to the ground at its range, where it lands, with a puff (drawn only: the rules fly it flat).

invites.hits.what: How many letters it takes to win a creature over by its level, and how fast its meter drains when not being hit.

decisions.quote: the invitation dropoff rate (the speed at which animals become less invited) is too fast
decisions.rest: 0.03 after 4 s, a full meter in about 33 s; it was states.json's 0.08 after 1.5 s, this knob unread

decisions.quote: I think we should remove the 0.5s cooldown between counted hits per creature - better to control this through the witch firing speed instead of having hits not register
let's change the drain rate to 2% instead of 3%
decisions.rest: 0.02 after 4 s, a full meter in about 50 s; hearts from her animals' blows fade the same, in one queue with the 💌s ("this should be the same speed as 💌s fade ... and they go in the same fade 'queue'")

invites.hits.notes: letters to fill it, by level (baby, young, adult); it drains drain of a full meter a second when not being hit, from config/states.json's affection.drainDelay seconds after the last [1]. Every letter that lands on an invitable creature counts [2]: how fast she invites is her firing rate (burst, burstGap, cooldown), nothing adaptive. Enraged creatures and legends block letters; scenery never stops them (Ed).

invites.fireSlow.what: her ground speed while firing, times this.

invites.inaccuracy.what: degrees either side of her aim each 💌 may go (a fixed hash of its number, so the same throws go the same ways); 0, dead straight, and a bag adds its own (config/wardrobe.json invitesAdd).

decisions.quote: For things with rapid rate of fire or shot-gun like clusters, we can also have accuracy/spread

invites.bloomPer.what: degrees more inaccuracy each volley while she keeps firing (the bloom); 0, none, and a bag adds its own.

invites.bloomDecay.what: degrees a second the bloom falls back by.

invites.bloomMax.what: the most degrees the bloom can reach.

invites.pierce.what: how many more creatures a 💌 flies on through after the first it lands on, each a hit as any letter's; 0, it stops at the first, and a bag adds its own (config/wardrobe.json invitesAdd).

decisions.quote: pierce, yes

invites.chain.what: how many hops a spent 💌 makes on to the nearest other invitable creature within chainRange metres (never one it has landed on, nor a stunned one), each a hit as any letter's; 0, none, and a bag adds its own (config/wardrobe.json invitesAdd).

decisions.quote: chain

invites.chainRange.what: how far (m) a chained 💌 looks for the next creature to hop to.

invites.linger.what: a 💌 that met no one rests where it came down this many seconds, fading over the last lingerFade, at most lingerMax at once (drawn only: it's no hit).

decisions.quote: invitations should sit on the ground for a little while before they fade away

invites.spin.what: How fast a 💌 spins in flight.

decisions.quote: the envelopes should spin like a frisbee

invites.spin.notes: a 💌 in flight lies flat and turns about the upright this many times a second (drawn only); when it lands it stops and lies flat.

invites.orbit.what: the 💌 ring circles a creature at scale times its body radius (movement.json bodies) plus gap metres, at least min, and at least height times its drawn height (to its top as drawn) plus gap, so it rings the creature you see at any size; wider still when it holds many.

decisions.quote: the orbits are smaller than the size of the creatures; their size should adjust depending on how large the creatures are
Invitation orbits are too tight around the creature
damage orbits are too wide, bring them in by around 30%
decisions.rest: scale 2 to 1.4, gap 1 to 0.7, min 2 to 1.4, height 0.9 to 0.63 (all x0.7); the soundsystem's 💥 ring 1.5 to 1.05 m outside it

invites.orbit.notes: A soundsystem's 💥 ring sits 1.5 gaps outside its radius.

invites.hard.what: the hard homing of the 💌s her Sentry and Slingshot hats throw: homing degrees a second, cone degrees either side it looks in, range metres it looks out to (was the legend buffs' charm, 420, 80 and 18).

invite.what: The old proximity chat, now replaced by the 💌 invite: she talked with the nearest creature in emoji.

decisions.rest: DESIGN.md, the leash; superseded by the 💌s, invites, and used only with invites.on false
losing a hit point is the cost

invite.notes: The old proximity chat [1]: on the ground, she talks by herself (no button: Ed, v244) to the nearest invitable creature within talkRange metres, and sticks with it; you chat in emoji for talkTime seconds (babies, young, adults), taking turns every turn seconds (babies, young, adults), then it is invited and leashed to you. Rising or moving further than cancelDistance stops it, and the chat's progress drains at decayRate of the rate it filled (0.5: half), so coming back soon picks up where it left off. Legends can't be invited: they give one unimpressed look. A legend gives her one unimpressed look for snubTime seconds per approach (not again till she's been beyond cancelDistance). Being hit doesn't set a chat back [2]. talkTime's fourth value is for legends let go on a knockout (wild legends still can't be invited).

win.what: The end of the route: after the last wave a pointer leads her to the remaining enraged creatures, then the victory lap.

decisions.quote: The end of the route
decisions.rest: rules/win.ts, docs/backlog/journey.md
a ring inside the conga's hid it from the ground

decisions.quote: Remove the end cards
decisions.rest: rules/guidance.ts; no card since Ed's

decisions.quote: when you're on the ground in the home area, the line should follow you

win.notes: The end of the route [1][2]: the last wave landed, a pointer to the enraged animal nearest the centre while any lives (enraged legends don't count; retarget: seconds between re-picks); none left, the victory lap: the pulse races back along the route to home at lapSpeed m/s, every stone it passes firing its fireworks; home reached, the night won: the dealt legends wake (bar any still enraged, which go back to sleep, their islands not found) and dance in place on its far side [3], north of the dancefloor beyond the conga, behind everything from the north-facing camera: on arcs legendGap m outside the conga's circle, legendRow m apart, legendSpace m between them, from due north out to legendArc degrees across, clear of the treehouse, the island's sigil flares on the dancefloor (drawn on over flareDraw s, held flare s), every other animal joins one conga line round it (congaSpeed m/s, congaGap m apart, a circle of at least congaRadius m, as big as the line needs), walking to its place at joinSpeed m/s (out of her sight, seen m off, simply there); once she reaches the party after the win (anywhere on the dancefloor, on foot or flying low: Ed, 2026-10-28), it settles: the guidance pins lead her home [4]. The conga follows her [5]: with follow on, while she's on the ground in the home area (not at the treehouse or in the treetops) the leader trails followLead m behind her along where she's walked and the rest follow single file congaGap apart, walking to their places at joinSpeed or followSpeed times her own speed, whichever is faster; anywhere else the line goes back round the dancefloor.

leash.length.what: how far a leashed creature roams from its leash point (you, or its sigil on the ground).

leash.runSpeed.what: how fast it hurries back when out of range (m/s).
leash.runSpeed.notes: how fast one out of range hurries back (m/s).

leash.pickRadius.what: how near a placed sigil you must be to pick it up.
leash.pickRadius.notes: how near (m) she picks up one of her own placed sigils.

leash.spacing.what: how close two sigils may be put down (keep it above pickRadius, or a blocked spot picks up instead of fizzling).
leash.spacing.notes: how far apart (m) sigils can be put down.

leash.runeRadius.what: how near (m) she picks up a happy creature's rune, a relic's sigil or her hat [1][2].

decisions.rest: both 25% further on: 3.5 to 4.375, 4.5 to 5.625

decisions.quote: Floor sigils of happy creatures and relics are difficult to pick up
decisions.rest: bigger than pickRadius, which stays under spacing, and less than a relic's sigilOffset, so standing on the relic itself doesn't

leash.hatHold.what: seconds she holds the sigil button on the ground, with nothing it picks up or puts down, to put her hat down at her feet (just a marker; a press over it puts it back on; rules/hat.ts putHat).

decisions.quote: If you are in ground mode and hold down the drop / pick up sigil button and there are no sigils to pick up, you put down your hat

leash.placedThrough.what: how bright a placed sigil shows where grass, bushes, trees or other scenery hide it (0 hidden, 1 as bright as in the open); never through the witch.

leash.sigilGlyph.what: How bright sigil glyphs are drawn, so they don't bloom into blobs on lit ground.

decisions.quote: it's their glow that makes them hard to see, not the pixellation

leash.sigilGlyph.notes: every sigil glyph from the leash atlas (placed, happy runes, the ghost, a relic's, her stack, the treetop projection, one walking home after a knockout) is drawn at sigilGlyph times its colour (0.5: under the bloom's threshold, so it doesn't bloom into a disc on lit ground; 1 as bright as before), and the soft halos under placed sigils, ready runes and relic sigils and round a relic in her stack at sigilHalo times their old strength (0: none).

leash.sigilBacking.what: A dark patch under every sigil on the ground, so it reads clearly.

quote: a dark patch directly underneath a sigil is quite helpful for making it more readable
the same width as the sigil, darker, edges not too smooth
decisions.rest: Bravo's o3

leash.sigilBacking.notes: under every sigil lying on the ground (placed, a happy creature's rune, the ghost, a relic's) a near-black disc in chunky 2-px cells with a lighter outer step, as wide as the glyph's own pixels times size, at dark (0: none), then the glyph painted opaque in its full neon at ink times how much it shows, under the dim added glyph (sigilGlyph).

leash.runeGap.what: a happy creature's rune lies south of it (down the screen), and a parked animal roams round a point the same way north of its sigil, by its size: its body radius, half the sigil with its backing, and runeGap metres between (rules/runeOffset.ts; it was a fixed restAbove, 5 m).

decisions.quote: Leashed animals should come to rest 10m above their placed sigil
decisions.rest: so it's easier to see and pick up

decisions.quote: the top of the sigil's background should be just below the animal's feet

leash.hex.what: Sigils are put down and picked up on a fixed hex grid on the ground, so a cluster of them reads cleanly.

decisions.quote: a cluster of placed sigils reads cleanly

leash.hex.notes: on the ground the sigil button works on a world-fixed hex grid, size metres between neighbouring cells (6 with the rank sigils, their ranks.hex; 4 before them, leash.spacing's density, as ?sigils=old still has it; 0: put down freely where she stands, as before). The cell nearest her decides: a sigil of hers in it, the press picks it up; free, a sigil goes down in its middle (never fizzling). Cells under a runestone or soundsystem (within stone metres of it, plus half a cell) or a home speaker (speaker metres) are skipped: the sigil goes down on the nearest free cell that isn't, within two cells, or not at all. Relic sigils and her hat go down where she stands, off the grid.

leash.runs.what: Holding the sigil button picks up, or puts down, sigils one after another as she runs.

decisions.quote: Pick up and place in runs

leash.runs.notes: with the sigil button held on since a press that picked a sigil up, she keeps picking up any sigil she runs over (her placed ones, happy creatures' runes, a relic's); held since a press that put one down, moving into each empty hex puts down the next (a press that did nothing starts no run, so holding E with nothing to do still puts her hat down). On the pad her hat is triangle's (placed or picked up), circle cycles the stack, L3 casts the broom's spell.

leash.runePull.what: on the ground, the nearest happy creature with its rune within radius (m) trots toward her at speed (m/s), stopping stop (m) from her, so its rune comes to her.

leash.grounded.what: Too many heavy creatures on her leash stop her taking off.

quote: One adult stops you taking off. Three young do.
if creatures are light or heavy you can extrapolate
decisions.rest: the numbers indicative

leash.grounded.notes: weight is the most the creatures following her may weigh, together, before she can't take off (their sigils in her stack, each at its leash.weight.levels weight times its species' strength, however near; parked ones at a sigil on the ground don't count, nor babies; 2 is one adult of normal strength, three young 2.4, two 1.6; 0 turns it off). Pressing rise she tries: she lifts a little and the leashes, taut and bright, pull her straight back down (drawn only: she never leaves the ground, so it's no dodge and spends no cooldown). Apart from the pull (weight below); once up she stays up, it only stops the next take-off.

leash.weight.what: How the creatures on her leash pull on her: slower moving away from them, slower to rise, and sinking in the treetops when heavily loaded.

decisions.quote: every sigil above your head pulls on you as well as attracting the animal; you find it slower to move in the opposite direction to where the leashes are, you are pulled off course, and rising to treetop is slower. And you're gradually pulled back down
decisions.rest: rules/leashWeight.ts
free in the treetops for 8 babies, 3 youths or 1 adult, and on the ground 5 youths or 2 adults (baby 0.3, youth 0.8, from 0.5 and 1)

decisions.quote: extra free allowance on the ground should be the equivalent of one adult
decisions.rest: the first few sigils' worth, so early play feels the same; on the ground, plus one adult's weight, levels' adult

leash.weight.notes: sigil weight [1]: each sigil in her stack (placed ones weigh nothing) pulls her toward its creature by how taut its leash is (0 within 0.85 of length, up to maxTension a leash length further, however far: a far traveller can't pin her) times its weight (levels: baby, young, adult, legend; times its species' combat.json strength) [2]. Less free [3], that's her load (weight units, a young on a taut leash being 1).

leash.weight.drag.what: moving away from the pull, that part of her speed is divided by 1 + drag x load (her input still steers).

leash.weight.drift.what: she drifts toward the pull at up to that share of her top speed, reached at an extreme load.

leash.weight.rise.what: rising takes 1 + rise x load times as long.

leash.weight.sink.what: Heavily loaded over the treetops she sinks toward the crowns, and lands if she stops.
leash.weight.sink.notes: over the treetops, loaded, she sinks by sink x load of the climb a second (at most sinkMax), to floor (of the climb, just over the crowns) while she flies on, and all the way down to land if she stops or her load reaches extreme; unloaded, she floats back up. The view reads leashLoad (rules/game.ts); the debug overlay shows it.

leash.weight.babyGround.what: a baby's weight on the ground (the treetops' is weight.levels[0]), so 8 fill either allowance; a baby's species strength doesn't count, and in the line its leash's tension is measured from its place in the line.

leash.babies.what: Her leashed babies follow her in single file and scatter out of the way while she's in a fight.

decisions.rest: docs/backlog/gameplay.md

decisions.quote: they should scatter further, e.g. outside of my camera view
decisions.rest: 55, past the view's farthest edge at the usual ground zoom, its top 50 m from her; kept on the island's land, and pulling on her not at all while scattered

leash.babies.notes: her leashed babies following her on the ground walk in single file along where she's been, in stack order (the stack's bottom one first), gap metres apart; while she's in a fight they scatter, scatter metres or a quarter more off to the side away from the first attacker [2], for the whole fight [3]: from the moment something goes for her or one of hers (closing in or winding up, not on the hit), the same way throughout, back into line once nothing has for calm seconds; one more than farAt metres from her (about off the screen) moves at farSpeed m/s, so it's with her in seconds.

leash.ranks.what: Leash sigils drawn as bare glyphs in their rank's colour (baby, youth, adult, legend) with embers rising off them, so ranks are easy to tell apart at a glance.

decisions.quote: larger sigils is good ... embers are good ... colours-for-rank is good; it's more important in rapid gameplay to be able to tell ranks apart than creatures
decisions.rest: after mocks 3 to 9; render/leash/ranks.ts

decisions.quote: go ahead and push all the new sigil work
decisions.rest: the default since; ?sigils=old turns them off and the hex grid back to 4 m

leash.ranks.notes: on [2], every leash sigil (her stack, placed sigils, happy runes, the ghost, the treetop projection, the bond) is its bare glyph, no ring or disc, glyph metres across on the ground, in its rank's colour (colours: baby, youth, adult, legend; the species' neon stays the world's: borders, stones, fireworks, dancefloor, holograms, chart), with embers rising off its strokes (embers.count at once, each size metres, rising rise metres, by rank; in her stack stack of that), under a dark shade in the glyph's own shape (not a disc); a youth in her stack shows two rows of round dots off to its right, one a berry it eats on the move (toEvolve less the last, eaten at a placed sigil), at most dotsPerRow a row, bright eaten and dim not, pulsing when ready; and the hex grid is hex metres (leash.hex.size).

bond.what: How a leashed creature shows its tie to its sigil: a glow at its feet, sparks, and a thread when the leash is strained.

decisions.quote: The curve on slack leashes should be higher than it is now
The arc of leashes should be higher
decisions.rest: doubled, 0.4 to 0.8 and the cap 4 to 8

bond.notes: how a creature shows its tie to its sigil (rim: a glow at its feet in the sigil's colour; sparks: one spark every sparkEvery seconds from sigil to creature, staggered; thread: a dotted line only under strain). The bond between her and her leashed creatures: rim, a glow at a creature's feet in its sigil's colour; sparks, one now and then from sigil to creature (every sparkEvery seconds, staggered); thread, a dotted line while a leash is under strain (past 0.85 of its length), bowing upward by threadArcSlack metres per metre of its length while slack, flattening to threadArcTaut as it goes taut [1][2], never more than threadArcMax metres.

leash.placeMotes.what: A sigil put down or picked up: its burst of motes rising in its colour (render/leash.ts, drawn in render/leash/combat.ts): count, size (m), bright (times its colour), rise and life (times the old height and length).

decisions.quote: Given current settings, the motes from sigils don't do much
decisions.rest: Ed, relayed; the art director's motes pass, #1398 (tools/shot/motes.cjs measures them)

leash.ranks.embers.bright.what: The embers rising off rank sigils (on the ground, in her stack, over the rune stones): their colour times this.

decisions.quote: Given current settings, the motes from sigils don't do much
decisions.rest: Ed, relayed; the art director's motes pass, #1398 (tools/shot/motes.cjs measures them)

leash.ranks.embers.crowd.what: Past this many of her sigils put down, each one's embers thinned by the square root, so a crowd of them isn't noise (0: never).

decisions.quote: Given current settings, the motes from sigils don't do much
decisions.rest: Ed, relayed; the art director's motes pass, #1398 (tools/shot/motes.cjs measures them)
